Slippery slope is not a fallacy. It is a type of argument. A fallacy is a failure in reasoning that renders an argument invalid. An appeal to authority, for example, is invalid because it references imaginary arguments outside of the discussion. You are assuming that the authority has better arguments than you without hearing them. An appeal to authority is an appeal to laziness by people who don't want to think.

That an action will have bad consequences is a very simple and valid argument. Slippery slope is just a type of bad consequence. It is the argument that movement in a direction will tend to continue in that direction to an unacceptable extent. In other words, that the consequence of the action is that it makes further action easier and that further action would be harmful. There is plenty of evidence and examples in history to support slippery slope arguments. Saying that you are making a "slippery slope" argument is not an argument. It is a simple statement of fact.
